value.value: Figure 5A: MUA/MPA 3/5/10 nm, 20/80/160 µg/mL, dye 30 min, readings 30/60/90 min, plotted 60 min, mean ± SD, p < 0.025. B: AUT/CYST, 0.5/3.5/20, otherwise same times, n=3 independent, p < 0.01. C: MUA 3/5/10 nm at 20/80/160 ±5 mM NAC. D: AUT 3/5/10 nm at explicitly labeled 0.5/5/20 ±5 mM NAC. C/D mean ± SD; no dose conversion between B and D. The positive-QD bar panels list 0.5/3.5/20 µg/mL in their legends/captions, but 5 and 10 nm CYST groups show only two bars; a 20 µg/mL result is not inferred for those groups.

value.value: NAC reduces measured ROS to baseline but does not rescue viability or ATP in the tested MUA/AUT conditions. Authors infer ROS-independent toxicity as one interpretation, while discussing mitochondrial injury as a hypothesis. This is not proof of a unique mechanism or a clinical safety ranking.

conflicts: Negative MUA/MPA: 20, 80, 160 µg/mL. Positive dose labels differ by assay/panel: general methods 0.5, 5, 20 µg/mL; Figures 2B, 3D, 4B, 5B use 0.5, 3.5, 20; Figure 3B images and Figures 5D/6 use their explicit labels. Never merge 3.5 and 5.
p.4 says MPA and CYST did not induce significant redox stress; p.10 and Table 4 report 5 nm MPA ROS increase, and Table 4 also marks one positive CYST 3 nm condition.
